    <div><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 10pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:DisclosureOfCompensationRelatedCostsShareBasedPaymentsTextBlock" id="ct-nonNumeric-f8fe594e-0f78-4b01-9b59-fdea264f2d2f" contextRef="Duration_1_1_2020_To_12_31_2020" escape="true" continuedAt="ct-nonNumeric-f8fe594e-0f78-4b01-9b59-fdea264f2d2f-continuation-0"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: bold;margin: 0;padding: 0;">12. font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: bold;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Accounting for Share-based Compensation</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 10pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.50in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">The Company recognizes share</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">-</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">based compensation expense in accordance with FASB ASC Topic&#160;718, &#8220;Stock Compensation&#8221; (&#8220;ASC 718&#8221;), for all share</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">-</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">based awards made to employees, non-employees and board members based on estimated fair values. ASC 718 requires companies to measure the cost of employee services incurred in exchange for the award of equity instruments based on the estimated fair value of the share</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">-</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">based award on the grant date. The expense is recognized over the requisite service period. The Company recognizes share-based award forfeitures as they occur.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 10pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.50in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">The Company uses a Black</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">-</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Scholes option</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">-</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">pricing model to value the Company&#8217;s option awards. Using this option</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">-</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">pricing model, the fair value of each employee and board member award is estimated on the grant date. The fair value is expensed on a straight</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">-</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">line basis over the vesting period. The option awards generally vest pro</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">-</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">rata annually. The expected volatility assumption is based on the volatility of the share price of comparable public companies. The expected life is determined using the &#8220;simplified method&#8221; permitted by Staff Accounting Bulletin Numbers&#160;107 and 110 (the midpoint between the term of the agreement and the weighted average vesting term). The risk</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">-</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">free interest rate is based on the implied yield on a U.S. Treasury security at a constant maturity with a remaining term equal to the expected term of the option granted. The dividend yield is zero, as the Company has never declared a cash dividend.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 10pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.50in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; Any payments made prior to FDA approval will be expensed as research and development. Due to the long</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">-</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">range nature of such commercial milestones, they are neither probable at this time nor predictable, and consequently are not included in the additional contingent milestone payment amount.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: bold;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Legal Contingencies</span></p></ix:continuation><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 10pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.50in;"><ix:continuation id="ct-nonNumeric-9eceaa98-e4a3-4d0e-9118-e8d25da6a171-continuation-1"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">The Company has been subject to various legal proceedings that arise from time to time in the ordinary course of its business. Although the Company believes that the various proceedings brought against it have been without merit, and that it has adequate product liability and other insurance to cover any claims, litigation is subject to many factors which are difficult to predict and there can be no assurance that the Company will not incur material costs in the resolution of legal matters. Should the Company determine that any future obligations exist, the Company will record an expense equal to the amount which is deemed probable and estimable. The Company has </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"><ix:nonFraction id="ct-nonFraction-4385adad-508d-45f0-8e31-460b001093dc" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyAccrualAtCarryingValue" contextRef="As_Of_12_31_2020" unitRef="Unit12" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">no</ix:nonFraction></span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> significant contingencies related to legal proceedings at December 31, 2020. </span></ix:continuation></p></div>
    <div><div class="footerContainer"><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 8pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: .001pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-align: center;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 8pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">&#160;</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: .001pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-align: center;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;" class="ctHeaderFooterPage">97</span></p></div><hr class="pageBreak" style="margin:18pt 0pt; ct-page-break: true; page-break-after: always;" /><div class="headerContainer"><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: .001pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;"><a href="#TableOfContents" style="text-decoration: none;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; white-space:pre-wrap; color: #0563C1;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: bold;margin: 0;padding: 0;text-decoration: underline;">Table of Contents</span></a></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 8pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: .001pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 8pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">&#160;</span></p></div></div>
    <div><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 10pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxDisclosureTextBlock" id="ct-nonNumeric-e602ece4-0410-47f1-81cd-ff6e245722d0" contextRef="Duration_1_1_2020_To_12_31_2020" escape="true" continuedAt="ct-nonNumeric-e602ece4-0410-47f1-81cd-ff6e245722d0-continuation-0"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: bold;margin: 0;padding: 0;">16. Income Taxes</span></ix:nonNumeric></p><ix:continuation id="ct-nonNumeric-e602ece4-0410-47f1-81cd-ff6e245722d0-continuation-0" continuedAt="ct-nonNumeric-e602ece4-0410-47f1-81cd-ff6e245722d0-continuation-1"><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 10pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.50in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">The Company accounts for income taxes in accordance with the asset and liability method of accounting for income taxes prescribed by FASB ASC Topic 740, &#8220;Accounting for Income Taxes&#8221; (&#8220;ASC&#160;740&#8221;). Under the asset and liability method of ASC 740, deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized for the future tax consequences attributable to differences between the financial statement carrying amounts of existing assets and liabilities and their respective tax basis and operating loss and tax credit carryforwards. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted tax rates expected to apply to the taxable income in the years in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled. Under ASC 740, the effect on deferred tax assets and liabilities of a change in tax rates is recognized in income in the period that includes the enactment dates.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 10pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.50in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">The Company follows FASB ASC Topic 740</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">-</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">10, &#8220;Accounting for Uncertainty in Income Taxes&#8221;, which prescribes a recognition threshold and measurement attribute for financial statement recognition and measurement of a tax position taken, or expected to be taken, in a tax return. For those benefits to be recognized, a tax position must be more likely than not to be sustained upon examination by taxing authorities. At&#160;December&#160;31, 2020 and 2019, the Company had&#160;no&#160;material uncertain tax positions to be accounted for in the financial statements. The Company recognizes interest and penalties, if any, related to unrecognized tax benefits in interest expense.&#160;The Company is obligated to file income tax returns in the U.S. federal jurisdiction and several U.S. states. Since the Company had losses in the past, all prior years that generated net operating loss carryforwards are open and subject to audit examination in relation to the net operating loss generated from those years.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 0;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.50in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">The Company recorded an income tax (benefit) expense of approximately $(</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"><ix:nonFraction id="ct-nonFraction-7e0ffb59-2d47-4c52-8e23-56c4e5f35b69" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit" contextRef="Duration_1_1_2020_To_12_31_2020" unitRef="Unit12" decimals="-5" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="6" sign="-">0.2</ix:nonFraction></span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; The deferred tax liability was initially recorded to account for the book vs. tax basis difference related to the goodwill intangible asset, also known as a &#8220;naked credit&#8221;. The deferred tax liability was excluded from sources of future taxable income, as the timing of its reversal cannot be predicted due to the indefinite life of the goodwill. In accordance with the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017, losses generated beginning with the 2018 tax year may be carried forward indefinitely for U.S. federal tax purposes, however losses were initially limited to offset 80% of taxable income in future years. Thus, 80% of the U.S. federal deferred tax liability related to goodwill was able to be used to offset the valuation allowance as of December 31, 2019. In accordance with the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security Act of 2020, however, losses generated in 2018 through 2020 may now offset 100% of taxable income in future years. Since the Company&#8217;s losses generated in 2018 through 2020 are greater than the book vs. tax basis difference related to goodwill, all of the U.S. federal deferred tax liability related to goodwill may be used to offset the valuation allowance as of December 31, 2020. This resulted in a reduction of the deferred tax liability of approximately $</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"><ix:nonFraction id="ct-nonFraction-b17c5265-c8e3-4b22-bf7b-022a8f10be25" name="kdmn:TaxCutsAndJobsActOf2017ChangeInTaxRateDeferredTaxLiabilityIncomeTaxExpenseBenefit" contextRef="Duration_1_1_2020_To_12_31_2020" unitRef="Unit12" decimals="-5" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="6">0.2</ix:nonFraction></span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> million during the year ended December 31, 2020. The Company files income tax returns in various states including New York, Massachusetts, and Pennsylvania, which provide for a 20-year loss carryforward before expiration. Thus, none of the U.S. state deferred tax liability related to goodwill may be used to offset the valuation allowance. As such, approximately $</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"><ix:nonFraction id="ct-nonFraction-9ba86be7-6837-47d2-9af5-7143c6450248" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxLiabilities" contextRef="As_Of_12_31_2020" unitRef="Unit12" decimals="-5" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="6">0.3</ix:nonFraction></span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; The Company experienced ownership changes under Section 382 of the Code in 2010, 2011 and 2016, but the Company did not reduce the gross deferred tax assets related to the NOL carryforwards because the limitations do not hinder the Company&#8217;s ability to potentially utilize all of the NOL carryforwards. The Company also experienced an ownership change under Section 382 of the Code in 2019, as a result of equity offerings. This ownership change reduced the Company&#8217;s ability to potentially utilize all of the NOL carryforwards and, consequently, resulted in a reduction to the Company&#8217;s gross deferred tax assets and related valuation allowance of $</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"><ix:nonFraction id="ct-nonFraction-9a95e817-88fa-42c9-8718-535efb21f638" name="kdmn:ReductionOfOperatingLossCarryforwards" contextRef="Duration_1_1_2020_To_12_31_2020" unitRef="Unit12" decimals="-5" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="6">125.2</ix:nonFraction></span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> million during November 2019. </span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 10pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.50in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">If an additional ownership change occurred in the future and if the Company earned net taxable income, the Company&#8217;s ability to use its pre</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">-</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">change NOLs to offset U.S. federal taxable income would be subject to these limitations, which could potentially result in increased future tax liability compared to the tax liability the Company would incur if its use of NOL carryforwards were not so limited. In addition, for state income, franchise and similar tax purposes, there may be periods during which the use of NOL carryforwards is suspended or otherwise limited, which could accelerate or permanently increase the Company&#8217;s state income, franchise or similar taxes. </span></p></ix:continuation><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 10pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.50in;"><ix:continuation id="ct-nonNumeric-e602ece4-0410-47f1-81cd-ff6e245722d0-continuation-2"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">In accordance with ASC 740, &#8220;Income Taxes,&#8221; the Company recorded a valuation allowance to fully offset the gross deferred tax asset, because it is more likely than not that the Company will not realize future benefits associated with these deferred tax assets at December&#160;31, 2020 and 2019. The change in deferred tax liability has been recognized as an income tax expense and benefit in the consolidated statements of operations for the years ended December 31, 2020 and 2019, respectively.</span></ix:continuation></p></div>
